s: PoHo Base remembers every project on your computer and where you stopped in each AI chat, and puts you back in with one click.
x: PoHo Base is the place you return to work. It knows the projects on your computer, remembers where you stopped in each one, in any AI coding tool, and takes you back there in one click. It works fully without AI. There is no account, nothing to download besides the app, and PoHo never uploads your source files. Only with your own Claude key does it send short excerpts (README, CLAUDE.md, file names, your prompts and the last replies) to Claude. Find Your projects are already there. PoHo looks only in the folders you allow, or in the folders where your AI tools worked, and makes a page for each project from what is really on disk: its README, stack, scripts, git branch, last commit and uncommitted changes. Press Ctrl P in the app, or Alt+Space from anywhere, to jump to any project or to something you once asked an AI. Remember PoHo reads the chat history of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode, and the plans and task lists Antigravity writes. For every project it keeps: what you asked, and which files changed; what was left open; time and tokens spent with AI. It keeps a copy even after the AI tool deletes its old chats. Home always starts with the project you were last in and where you stopped. Return Continue reopens the exact chat where it ended, in your editor or a terminal. Pick up with … starts any installed AI tool with a note of where the work stopped, so you can switch tools without explaining everything again. New Claude Code and Cursor chats can start already knowing the project, your last session and what is left. See [Connect your AI tools](../get starte

s: Download the zip, run PoHo Base.exe once, and it installs itself for your Windows user with no admin rights.
x: Download PoHo Base as a zip, open PoHo Base.exe from it, and click Accept and install . PoHo installs itself for your Windows user, with Desktop and Start menu shortcuts. You do not need admin rights or an account. PoHo Base runs on Windows 10 and 11. It is free. Steps 1. Download [PoHo Base win x64.zip](https://github.com/ChefMiki/poho base releases/releases/latest/download/PoHo Base win x64.zip). This link always gets the newest version. 2. Unzip it anywhere, for example in your Downloads folder. 3. Open the PoHo Base folder and double click PoHo Base.exe . 4. If Windows shows “Windows protected your PC”, click More info , then Run anyway . 5. On Welcome to PoHo Base , choose what PoHo may do. See [The first start](first start.md). 6. Tick I have read and accept the Terms of Use and the Privacy Notice . 7. Click Accept and install . The window closes and the installed PoHo opens. You can now delete the downloaded zip and folder. Note: Windows may warn you because PoHo Base is a new app and is not code signed. The updates PoHo installs later are signed by its developer, and PoHo refuses any that are not. See [Updates and beta versions](updates.md). Where it goes PoHo installs into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\PoHo Base , inside your own user folder. It adds a Desktop shortcut and a Start menu shortcut. Nothing else on the computer changes, and it never touches your project files. If you already have PoHo installed Running a newer download installs over the old copy: PoHo asks the running one to close first. Your projects, notes and memory stay. Remove it Open Settings → Privac

s: Choose what PoHo may read, accept the terms, then let PoHo find your AI work or pick your project folders yourself.
x: The first time PoHo opens, you choose what it may do, and then which folders it may look in. PoHo reads nothing on your computer until you accept. 1. Choose what PoHo may do The Welcome to PoHo Base screen has a switch for each permission. All are on by default; turn off any you do not want. Read my AI coding sessions : the chat history of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Antigravity on this computer, so PoHo can show where you stopped and continue those chats. Take pictures of my apps’ windows : only a project’s own app while it is open, never editors, terminals or browsers. Check my projects’ websites : loads each project’s public website to take a picture and see that it responds. Tell AI agents where I stopped : new Claude Code and Cursor chats start knowing the project and what is left. This adds a small hook to their settings. See [Connect your AI tools](connect ai tools.md). Start with Windows : PoHo opens quietly in the tray when you sign in. This switch appears only in the installed app; when you start from the download, turn it on later in Settings → General . Then tick I have read and accept the Terms of Use and the Privacy Notice . Click either name to read it right there. Click Accept and install (when you started from the download, see [Install PoHo](install.md)) or Accept and continue . Tip: You can change these choices any time: the first three in Settings → Privacy & safety → What PoHo may do , briefings in Settings → AI agents , and Start with Windows in Settings → General . 2. Show PoHo your projects Next, PoHo offers two ways in: Find my AI

s: Add a project folder, or a folder that holds many projects, and PoHo finds the projects inside. It never searches your drives on its own.
x: Click Add folder on the Projects page, then drop folders in or click to choose them. PoHo finds the projects inside and adds a page for each. It only looks in folders you add, and never searches your drives on its own. Add a folder 1. Open Projects in the top bar. 2. Click Add folder . 3. Drop one or more folders on Add project folders , or click the folder button to choose them. You can add a single project, or a folder that holds many projects, such as C:\Users\you\code . PoHo looks inside for git repos and project files like package.json , pyproject.toml , Cargo.toml , go.mod , CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md . Each one becomes a project. PoHo reads project names, READMEs and git status. Nothing is uploaded. Folders where your AI worked When an AI tool works in a folder PoHo does not know yet, a small card appears at the bottom right: “Claude Code worked in my app”. Click Add to PoHo to add it as one project, or Don’t add to stop being asked about it. If PoHo lists a lot of folders (more than 150), it offers Choose folders so you can keep only the ones where you worked with AI, or Keep all . Find projects you added later PoHo looks again every 15 minutes and when you start it. To look right now, open ⚙ → Look for new projects . Manage your folders Open Settings → Projects & folders . Folders PoHo reads lists every folder, with how many projects PoHo found in it. Add folder adds another. The X next to a folder ( Stop watching this folder ) makes PoHo forget that folder’s projects. The files on disk are not touched. Keep only my AI work keeps only the folders where you worked with

s: PoHo remembers chats from your AI coding tools on its own; connect Claude Code and Cursor so new chats start knowing where you stopped.
x: Most AI tools need no setup: PoHo reads the chats they save on your computer. Connect Claude Code and Cursor as well, and every new chat in them starts already knowing the project and where you stopped. What works on its own With Read my AI coding sessions on (see [The first start](first start.md)), PoHo reads the chat history of: Claude Code Codex Gemini CLI OpenCode Antigravity (its plans, task lists and walkthroughs; not its conversations) Each chat shows up on its project’s page under Sessions . Nothing is uploaded. Tip: Claude Code deletes its old chats after 30 days by default. PoHo keeps a copy, so you can still find what you asked. Connect Claude Code and Cursor Connecting adds a small hook to the tool’s settings. When you start a new chat, the AI gets a short briefing: what the project is, your last session in any tool, what was left open, uncommitted files and your notes. PoHo also sees when the AI is waiting for you or has finished, for Live now on Home and for notifications. 1. On Home, find the Your tools card. 2. Click Connect next to Claude Code or Cursor . 3. Read what it does, then click Connect . You can also do it in Settings → AI agents → Agent memory , under Briefing at the start of a session : click Connect next to Claude Code or Cursor Agent . Disconnect removes PoHo’s hook again. Let your AI ask PoHo In the same place, under PoHo as a tool the agent can ask , you can connect Claude Code , Cursor and Codex . The AI can then ask PoHo where you stopped on a project, which earlier session dealt with something, and which of your projects use a technology

s: PoHo downloads signed updates on its own; restart to use one, go back one version if it gives you trouble, or get beta versions first.
x: PoHo updates itself. When a new version is downloaded and checked, a card says “PoHo Base X is ready”: click Restart now , or simply keep working and it installs when you quit. How updates arrive PoHo looks for a new version a minute after it starts and then every 30 minutes. It downloads the update in the background and checks it before offering it. Signed updates: every update is signed by PoHo’s developer. An update that is not signed, or was changed on the way, is refused. When it is ready you get the card and a desktop notification. Click Restart now to switch at once, or close the card: the update installs the next time PoHo quits. If PoHo waits in the tray with nothing running and no AI chat going, it can install the update on its own and stay in the tray. Before every switch, PoHo copies its own memory (projects, notes, sessions), so nothing is lost. After an update, What’s new in PoHo Base shows once, with every change since the version you had. Check by hand 1. Open Settings → Updates . 2. Click Check for updates . The line under the version says what happened, for example “You have the newest version.” When an update is ready, the button becomes Restart now , and the Updates page shows a green dot. Go back one version If a new version gives you trouble: 1. Open Settings → Updates . 2. Under Go back , click Go back next to Go back to version X . 3. Confirm. PoHo restarts on the older version. Your projects, notes and memory stay. The version you left is skipped until a newer one comes out. Note: Go back appears only after an update, and goes back one version. Get

t: See what a project is running
s: While a project runs, the centre of its map comes alive with its processes, memory, CPU and ports, and shows when an AI tool is working.
x: Open a project’s page and look at the Map tab. While anything runs for that project, the centre of the map comes alive: a green ring breathes around it, and one line says how many processes run, how much memory they use and how much CPU. What you see Click the centre of the map, or Tab to it and press Enter , to open its details: Memory : what the project’s processes use together. CPU : their share of this computer. Ports : the ports they listen on. AI now : the AI tools working in the project right now. Open in : the editors that have the project open. The list of processes, each with its CPU, memory and port. A process using half the CPU or more is marked in amber. The numbers refresh every few seconds while the map is open and PoHo’s window is visible. What counts as the project’s PoHo looks at the folder each process works in. A process belongs to the project when: it works inside the project folder, or its command line names the folder, or it was started by one of those processes. So a dev server you started yourself in a terminal ( npm run dev , node server.js , python app.py ) counts, and so does Claude Code running in a terminal. You don’t need to press Run first. A server started with Run counts too. What doesn’t count: A terminal that only sits in the folder. What you start in it does count. PoHo itself, git and Windows’ own processes. Editors such as Cursor and VS Code. One editor serves many projects, so they are named under Open in , not counted. When an AI tool is working The centre also comes alive while an AI tool works in the project, even when no process

t: What your AI is told when a chat starts
s: New Claude Code and Cursor chats get a short briefing from PoHo on the project and where you stopped; turn it on or off per tool.
x: When you start a new chat in Claude Code or Cursor, PoHo hands the AI a short briefing about the project, so you don’t have to explain where you stopped. You turn it on once per tool in Settings → AI agents → Agent memory . What the briefing contains Only facts PoHo already knows about the project, and only the lines it has something for: what the project is your last AI session, from any tool, with its summary what was left open last time commits made since that session files that are not committed yet your own notes on the project how to run it skills that fit this project , so the AI can use one when the task matches ([Skills that fit a project](../skills/skills for a project.md)) a few earlier sessions It ends by telling the AI that the files in the repository are the source of truth. The briefing is background, not orders. Claude Code also gets a fresh briefing right after it compacts a long conversation. Turn it on or off 1. Open Settings (Ctrl+,) and go to AI agents . 2. Under Agent memory , find Briefing at the start of a session . 3. Click Connect next to Claude Code or Cursor Agent . Click Disconnect to turn it off. The welcome screen offers the same choice as Tell AI agents where I stopped . Note: Connecting works only in the installed app. Chats that are already open don’t get the briefing; start a new one. What PoHo changes on your computer PoHo adds its own small hook to Claude Code’s settings ( ~/.claude/settings.json ) and to Cursor’s hooks file ( ~/.cursor/hooks.json ). Hooks from you or other tools stay as they are, and PoHo keeps a one time backup of eac

s: Use several Claude Code accounts, pick one per project, work side by side in lanes, and see how much of your Claude limit is left.
x: PoHo can keep several Claude Code accounts on one computer, for example work, personal and a client, and lets you pick one per project. The Claude limit card on Home shows how much of your 5 hour window is used. Add an account 1. Open Settings (Ctrl+,) and go to AI agents . 2. Under Claude accounts , type a name in Account name, e.g. Work . 3. Click Add account . 4. Claude Code opens in a terminal. Sign in there with that account. Back in PoHo, the account shows its email (or Signed in ) and Ready . Each account keeps its own login and history. The x removes an account from PoHo only; its login folder stays on disk. Note: Each account follows its own plan and Anthropic’s terms. Use accounts for separate work, not to get around usage limits. Pick the account for a project 1. Open the project and go to the Sessions tab. 2. In the Claude accounts panel, choose an account under This project uses . New chats on that project start with that account. Continuing an old chat always uses the account it was made with. Accounts other than your main one open in a terminal, because the editor extension only knows the main account. The panel appears once you have more than one account. Lanes: two accounts on one project In a git project, New lane gives an account its own copy of the code on its own branch, inside a .lanes folder in the project, so accounts never overwrite each other. Open starts Claude in that lane. Merge brings the lane’s commits back into your main branch; PoHo refuses if there are uncommitted changes and never leaves a half finished merge. A warning if some plugins are installed for this project only and won’t load where the chat runs. Install them for all projects to use them there. Everything it loads folds out the full list. If the chat wasn’t running, PoHo simply opens it. Note: If the AI is answering right now, that answer stops. In Cursor or VS Code the chat stays on screen; your next message continues it with everything new. Tip: In a Claude Code chat that is open, you can also type /reload plugins to pick up new plugins. What PoHo touches Only the processes running that one chat. PoHo never edits the conversation and never changes your skills or plugins. s: How PoHo picks the skills that suit a project, and how to tell your AI about them.

s: PoHo never deletes your files; it only forgets its own memory, and changes project files only when you click.
x: PoHo never deletes your files, and it has no button that does. When you remove something in PoHo, it only forgets its own memory; your folders stay exactly where they are. Forgetting is not deleting Archive project (project page → Setup ): the project leaves your lists. The files stay where they are and you can bring it back any time with Restore from archive . Remove from PoHo… (the project’s … menu): PoHo stops showing it on Home, in the lists and in search. It moves to Archived in Projects, with its notes and history. Its files on your disk are not touched. Stop watching this folder ( Settings → Projects & folders ): PoHo forgets the projects in that folder. Files on disk are not touched. Start over ( Settings → Privacy & safety ): PoHo forgets its project list, notes, session memory and settings and opens at the welcome screen. A copy of its memory is kept in a backup folder. Uninstall PoHo Base : removes the app, its shortcuts, start with Windows, its hooks and PoHo as a tool in your AI agents. Your project files are never touched. See [Questions people ask](../faq/faq.md how do i uninstall poho). Changes it makes only when you click Apart from snapshots, which it keeps hidden in the project’s .git folder, PoHo touches a project’s files only when you ask it to: adding notes for your AI to CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md ; adding .gitignore lines for .env files; putting a project on GitHub (adds a .gitignore and a first commit, then pushes to your own account); making or merging a lane for another Claude account (a .lanes folder with its own branch); restoring files from a sna

s: PoHo saves your project before every AI session, so you can put back any file an agent broke.
x: Before an AI session starts, PoHo saves your project, so you can put back anything an agent broke, one file or all of them. You don’t have to do anything: it happens on its own for every project that uses git. When a snapshot is taken When you continue or start a chat from PoHo. When Claude Code or Cursor starts a session on its own, if you connected them in Settings → AI agents . When you click Save snapshot now . Where snapshots live Snapshots are hidden inside the project’s own .git folder. They never change your files, branches or history, and a normal git push doesn’t send them. PoHo keeps the newest 30. .env files are never saved in a snapshot, and never restored over. Files your .gitignore leaves out, such as node modules , aren’t saved either. See what changed and put files back 1. Open the project and go to Setup . 2. In Snapshots , click a snapshot to see the files that changed since. 3. Click Restore next to one file, or Restore all . 4. Confirm. You can also open a session on the Sessions tab and fold open What this session changed . When you restore, PoHo saves the current state first, so you can undo it. If that safety snapshot can’t be made, nothing is restored. Files that are new since the snapshot are left as they are. When there is no snapshot The project doesn’t use git. Snapshots need git. Nothing changed since the last snapshot. More than 5,000 untracked files , often a node modules folder without a .gitignore . The project’s git settings name a program to run. PoHo doesn’t touch such a repository, to keep you safe. x: PoHo lists only skills in the folders it knows about. Open Projects → Skills , scroll down and open Where PoHo looked : it lists every folder PoHo searched and how many skills it found in each. Where PoHo looks A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file in it. PoHo looks in: Your skills folders: ~/.claude/skills , ~/.agents/skills , ~/.cursor/skills and ~/.codex/skills . s: Why “AI working” or Live now may stay empty, and what to check.
x: PoHo shows your AI as working while its chat file keeps changing, and for 3 minutes after the last change. Check that PoHo may read your AI sessions, that the chat runs in a project PoHo knows, and that the briefing is connected. How PoHo knows The chat file. About every 10 seconds, PoHo checks the chat files of recent sessions. If one changed in the last 3 minutes, the AI counts as working. This works for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode. The briefing connection. When it is connected, Claude Code and Cursor also tell PoHo the moment they wait for you or finish. Claude Code’s finish ends “working” at once. You see it on Home : the AI working chip on the project, and the Live now card. What to check 1. PoHo may read your AI sessions. Chats that were already open don’t pick up a new connection. Things that are normal It says finished while the AI is thinking. If the AI writes nothing for 3 minutes, for example during a long command, PoHo shows it as finished. Cursor never shows “waiting for you”. Cursor does not report it. s: When the project map shows something running, and why it may stay quiet.
x: The map comes alive only while it is open and PoHo’s window is visible. Then PoHo checks every 5 seconds what runs in the project; if it finds a program working there, an AI working or the dev server running, the centre turns green and breathes. How PoHo finds what runs in a project A program counts for a project when: it works in the project folder (its current folder is the project or a folder inside it), or its command line or program path names the project folder, or it belongs to an AI chat PoHo knows, plus every program those start. So a dev server you start in a terminal ( node server.js , python app.py ) counts even if you didn’t start it from PoHo. These never count: PoHo itself, a terminal that only sits in the folder (what it starts does count), git and Windows system programs. Editors such as VS Code or Cursor are shown under “Open in” instead, because one editor serves many projects. An AI that PoHo sees working, from its chat file or the briefing connection, also makes the centre come alive, even when its program isn’t found. See [PoHo doesn’t show my AI working](../troubleshooting/ai not shown.md). Why it may stay quiet The map is not open, or PoHo is minimised. PoHo looks only while you watch. The program runs somewhere else. If it started in another folder and doesn’t name the project folder, PoHo can’t tell it belongs to the project. PowerShell is limited on your computer. PoHo asks Windows through PowerShell. On computers that limit PowerShell (Constrained Language Mode, often set by a company), PoHo can’t read each program’s current folder; it still fin

s: How often PoHo looks for updates, how to check now, and why an update may not install.
x: PoHo looks for a new version a minute after it starts and then every 30 minutes. To check now, open Settings → Updates and click Check for updates . Check now 1. Open Settings and more (the gear in the top bar) → Settings . 2. Go to Updates . 3. Click Check for updates . The line under your version tells you what happened: “You have the newest version.” “<version is downloaded and checked. It installs when PoHo restarts.” Click Restart now , or it installs when you quit. An error, such as “This release is not signed, so PoHo will not install it.” When PoHo sits in the tray with nothing running, it can also install a ready update quietly by itself. Why an update may not arrive It is a beta. New versions go to beta users first. To get them too, turn on Get beta versions first in Settings → Updates . Without it, you get only stable versions. You went back from that version. After Go back to version X , PoHo skips the version you left until a newer one comes out. It is not signed, or it was changed on the way. PoHo installs only updates signed by its developer and refuses anything else. The download was damaged. PoHo refuses it; check again later. GitHub can’t be reached. Updates come from PoHo’s releases on GitHub. Without internet, PoHo can’t check. Note: Before every update, PoHo copies your PoHo data. Your projects, notes and memory stay. If a new version gives you trouble, use Go back in Settings → Updates . See also [Updates and beta versions](../get started/updates.md).

s: Why Windows may warn about PoHo, and what to do if it happens.
x: If Windows shows a warning or refuses to start PoHo, first make sure you downloaded it from PoHo’s official download link. Then use Windows’ own dialog to allow it, or report the problem to us. Why it can happen Windows has guards, such as SmartScreen and Smart App Control , that can warn about or stop programs downloaded from the internet. What PoHo is: PoHo Base.exe is the standard Electron program, only renamed. PoHo’s own code sits next to it. The exe has no Windows code signature of PoHo’s own. Updates never change PoHo Base.exe . They replace only PoHo’s code, and only when it is signed by PoHo’s developer. PoHo checks that signature itself; Windows does not. If Windows warns you 1. Check where the file came from. The download is PoHo Base win x64.zip from PoHo’s releases on GitHub (the Download button on PoHo’s website). 2. Unpack the zip, then start PoHo Base.exe . 3. If SmartScreen shows “Windows protected your PC”, click More info , then Run anyway . After the first start, PoHo installs itself for your user ( Accept and install ) and makes Desktop and Start menu shortcuts. If Smart App Control blocks it Please don’t turn off Windows protection to get past it. Tell us instead: open an issue on PoHo’s releases page on GitHub ( github.com/ChefMiki/poho base releases ) with your Windows version and the exact message. If PoHo starts, you can use [Report a problem](../troubleshooting/report a problem.md). Note: PoHo installs into your own user folder, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\PoHo Base .

s: Send a bug, an idea or a question from inside PoHo, and see exactly what is sent.
x: Open Settings and more (the gear in the top bar) → Report a bug . Describe what happened, add a screenshot if it helps, and click Send . Send a report 1. Click the gear in the top bar, then Report a bug . 2. Pick Bug , Idea or Question . 3. Write a Title and what happened. For a bug, add How to make it happen again if you can. 4. Add screenshots with Add screenshot , paste them with Ctrl+V, or drag them in (up to 5 PNG, JPEG or WebP images, 2 MB each). 5. Click Send , or Copy instead to copy the report and send it your own way. The note above the buttons tells you where the report goes. Today that is usually a GitHub issue you post yourself: PoHo opens it in your browser, filled in, and you press Submit there. It needs a free GitHub account. Screenshots are not added to the issue for you: drag them into it on GitHub. Warning: GitHub issues are public. Leave out anything private from your title, text and screenshots. What is sent Click What is sent to see every field before you send. With Include details about this computer on (the default), the report includes: PoHo’s version and how it is installed your Windows version, computer model, processor, memory, graphics and screen PoHo’s anonymous device ID, made when PoHo was installed how PoHo’s AI add on is set up, and how many projects and sessions PoHo knows recent errors from PoHo’s log Turn the switch off to send only what you wrote. How PoHo keeps it safe: Secrets such as keys, tokens and passwords are removed from the error log, your home folder is replaced with %USERPROFILE% , and file names are replaced with “…”. PoHo

s: Short answers about price, AI, privacy, platforms, your files, your data, uninstalling and more.
x: Is PoHo free? Yes. PoHo Base is a free preview for personal use. It is early software, so it may change or have bugs. Do I need AI to use it? No. Every core feature works without AI: finding projects, remembering sessions, continuing chats, snapshots and notes. The AI add on (free local AI through Ollama, or your own Claude key) only adds summaries in plain words. See [The AI add on](../connect/ai add on.md). Does it upload my code? Not unless you ask. Putting a project on GitHub pushes it to your own account. With your own Claude key, the AI add on sends Anthropic short excerpts (the README, CLAUDE.md , file names, what you asked your AI and its last replies), never whole source files. Local AI through Ollama keeps everything on this computer. There is no analytics or telemetry. See [Privacy in short](../safety/privacy.md). Does it work on Mac or Linux? No. PoHo Base is for Windows 10 and 11. Which AI tools does it work with? PoHo remembers sessions from Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode, and the plans and task lists Antigravity writes. Claude Code and Cursor can get a briefing at the start of every chat, and Claude Code, Cursor and Codex can ask PoHo questions as a tool. See [Connect your AI tools](../get started/connect ai tools.md). Will it change or delete my files? PoHo never deletes your files. It changes a project’s files only when you click, for example to add notes to CLAUDE.md or restore a file from a snapshot. See [What PoHo never does](../safety/never deletes.md). Where is my data? On this computer, in %APPDATA%\PoHo Base . Snapshots live in each pro
